title: SemPA: Improving Sentence Embeddings of Large Language Models through Semantic Preference Alignment
subcategory: preference optimisation (sentence-level DPO) of decoder LLMs for embeddings
task: Sentence embeddings (STS) while preserving generation ability
problem: Prompt-based LLM embeddings are not optimised, while architecture changes (bidirectional attention, contrastive fine-tuning) damage the LLM's generative ability.
architecture: Sentence-level Direct Preference Optimization on a paraphrase-generation task built from NLI triplets (entailment = preferred, contradiction = rejected) with LoRA; embedding read from the last token of a PromptEOL-style template; theoretical link between DPO and contrastive learning under the Plackett-Luce model.
key_results: Average STS Spearman 78.10 with LLaMA3-8B vs 75.34 for Token Prepending and 71.90 for PromptEOL.
With LLaMA2-7B: 77.69 vs 77.19 for Token Prepending.
strengths: Keeps generative capability of the LLM (evaluated on general LLM benchmarks).
Formal connection between DPO and contrastive learning.

limitations.text: Preliminary, lightweight experiments; dataset quantity/quality and prompt optimisation not explored.
Pairwise DPO uses only binary comparisons; listwise preference optimisation could exploit more ranking information.
